classification.difficultyReason: Locate the right angle and write the Pythagoras equation, including one triangle with only vertex names. It is simpler than p7-q1's cylinder and semicircle parts, but needs more than checking given numbers.

content.prompt:
Write an equation describing the relationship between the sides of these right-angled triangles.

$\text{side}^{2}+\text{side}^{2}=\text{hypotenuse}^{2}$

answer.worked:
The side opposite the right angle is $g$.
$$e^{2}+f^{2}=g^{2}$$

The hypotenuse is $XZ$, opposite the right angle at $Y$.
$$XY^{2}+YZ^{2}=XZ^{2}$$

The side opposite the right angle is $k$.
$$8^{2}+15^{2}=k^{2}$$
